about: How each pull request was checked, as recorded in its description on GitHub. These numbers are not computed at build time; each entry links to its source. Today's totals are in test-counts.json, written by scripts/count_tests.ts.

prs.title: Model, tokenizer, tests and CI
prs.check: 28 deliberately broken versions of the model and tokenizer (wrong attention scaling, missing LayerNorm, no position embeddings, temperature mistakes and more): every one makes a test fail.

prs.title: Data pipeline for the three books
prs.check: 12 kinds of deliberate damage to the data (swapped verses, a Yusuf Ali verse in place of Pickthall's, a stray digit, a truncated verse and more): the tests catch all 12. The pipeline gives byte-identical output on every run.

prs.title: Training, sampling, and the eval harness
prs.check: 58 hand-written mutants of the training loop, sampling, eval reports and suffix array: each one makes at least one test fail. A 300-step smoke run of the full model, and a killed run that resumed at the right step.

prs.title: Training results, eval report and samples
prs.check: A test keeps the README's result tables in sync with the eval JSON, so a number cannot drift from its source.

prs.title: The verse search and the parallels
prs.check: Every message from the independent blind reviews is a regression test, and every stored crisis message is also run as if the rules had missed it, to check what the topic suggestions alone would offer. A fuzz test checks that no suggestion ever contains a verse, a reference or verse text.

prs.title: This website
prs.check: The browser's verse search gives the same JSON as the Python one on every fixture and on thousands of generated messages. The forward pass matches PyTorch's logits within 1e-4, and greedy generation matches it token for token.

ci: GitHub Actions runs the Python tests on every pull request and every push to main, with CPU-only PyTorch, and a second job for this website: install, typecheck, unit tests, build and browser tests.
